in the installed ray 2.55.1, ray/rllib/core/learner/torch/torch_learner.py TorchLearner._set_optimizer_state calls self._named_optimizers[name].load_state_dict(convert_to_torch_tensor(state_dict['state'], device=self._device))

CAUSAL_INFERENCE.definition: the mechanism that, in our judgement, connects those facts. It is an inference, not a measurement.
CAUSAL_INFERENCE.claim: the eight differences are artefacts of comparing the checkpoint BEFORE RLlib's conversion against the live optimizer AFTER it. They are not evidence about the restore.
supporting_steps: the object the audit reads off the pickle, entry['state'], is precisely the argument RLlib passes to convert_to_torch_tensor; the live optimizer is precisely what load_state_dict produced from the converted copy
a Python bool leaf reaches the else branch of mapping and becomes torch.from_numpy(np.asarray(False)), a zero-dimensional tensor of dtype bool; it is not floating point, so it is not downcast

a Python float leaf becomes a zero-dimensional float64 tensor and is then downcast by tensor.float() to float32, which is why 0.9 reads back as 0.8999999761581421, 0.999 as 0.9990000128746033 and 1e-08 as 9.99999993922529e-09

rev2's normalisation puts a Python bool in the typed ('prim','bool',value) branch, evaluated FIRST, and puts a zero-dimensional tensor in the ('scalar', value) branch; the two branches can never compare equal, which is exactly the 'prim vs scalar' text of the five boolean differences
the moments were already numpy float32 on the checkpoint side, so the conversion is a no-op for them, which is why 12 of 12 agree byte for byte

weight_decay is a Python int and the params entries are Python ints; rev2's rule 4 sends both a Python int and a zero-dimensional int tensor to ('scalar', value), so they compared equal and never appeared among the differences
foreach and fused are None on both sides and mapping passes None through unchanged, so they compared equal

lr does not appear among the differences because the original _reapply_optimizer_learning_rate runs BEFORE the capture, as rev1 requires, and overwrites param_groups lr with the exact Python float 1e-4
CAUSAL_INFERENCE.measured_support: the architect independently read the installed implementation and confirmed both clauses: convert_to_torch_tensor preserves existing tensors, routes every non-None leaf through numpy into torch, downcasts every floating tensor except float16 to float32, and then moves to the target device. This report was verified in first person against the same installed files before this amendment was written.

correction_3_the_comparison_is_canonical.the_rule: R9 compares the checkpoint and the live optimizer under the SAME post-RLlib-conversion semantics. Both sides are passed through the conversion RLlib itself performs, and only the results are compared.
correction_3_the_comparison_is_canonical.not_a_tolerance: no epsilon, no relative tolerance, no approximate equality and no numeric comparison of any kind is introduced. After canonicalisation the comparison is still exact: dtype, shape and the sha256 of the C-order bytes of every leaf.
correction_3_the_comparison_is_canonical.why_canonicalising_BOTH_sides_and_not_on: converting only the checkpoint would leave the live side at the mercy of whatever torch's load_state_dict did to it afterwards. Converting both makes the comparison a comparison of fixed points of one function, which is what 'the same semantics' has to mean if it is to mean anything.

the_conversion.function: ray.rllib.utils.torch_utils.convert_to_torch_tensor, IMPORTED from the installed library and never reimplemented
the_conversion.arguments: the whole optimizer state_dict of each side, with device taken from the live learner's own _device, so the canonical form is produced on the device the restore actually used
the_conversion.why_import_and_not_copy: a reimplementation could drift from the library. Importing the exact function makes 'the exact conversion semantics RLlib uses' literally true rather than approximately true.
fail_closed_on_drift: the source of TorchLearner._set_optimizer_state must still contain the literal call convert_to_torch_tensor(state_dict["state"], device=self._device); if it does not, the audit fails closed rather than canonicalising through a path RLlib no longer takes
convert_to_torch_tensor must still accept a device parameter; if it does not, the audit fails closed

the conversion must be a FIXED POINT on both sides: canonical(convert(x)) must equal canonical(convert(convert(x))). If applying the conversion twice moves either side, the canonicalisation is not idempotent, the argument above does not hold, and the audit fails closed

the_canonical_node.order_is_significant: the branches are evaluated in this order and the order is part of the specification
the_canonical_node.1_None: ('none',). convert_to_torch_tensor passes None through, so None survives canonicalisation and a None that became a value is still caught.
the_canonical_node.2_str: ('str', value). Strings are not leaves of an optimizer state_dict; the branch exists so an unexpected one is recorded rather than swallowed.
the_canonical_node.3_torch_tensor_of_any_rank_including_zer: ('t', dtype string with the 'torch.' prefix stripped, shape tuple, sha256 of the C-order bytes of the detached CPU copy). This ONE branch carries every scalar and every moment. It is where byte identity is enforced, and it is where dtype is preserved.
the_canonical_node.4_list_and_tuple: ('seq', [canonical items]). A tuple and a list with the same contents canonicalise equal, because betas survives the round trip as either.
the_canonical_node.5_dict: ('map', sorted list of (canonical key, canonical value)); keys are canonicalised as ('key', type name, value) so an integer key stays an integer key and can never collide with a string key.
the_canonical_node.6_anything_else: ('opaque', type name), which can never equal a real value on the other side, so an unrecognised type fails closed.

correction_3_the_comparison_is_canonical.why_zero_dimensional_tensors_are_NOT_col: rev2 collapsed them, for a good reason at the time: it was the only way to make the checkpoint's Python float step equal the live 0-D tensor step. Canonicalisation removes that need, because after the conversion BOTH sides hold a 0-D tensor. Keeping them as typed tensors is what restores the discrimination rev2 had to give up: a bool and a numeric zero now differ by dtype, not by a branch name.
correction_3_the_comparison_is_canonical.declared_consequence_carried_over_from_r: the original _reapply_optimizer_learning_rate still runs FIRST and still overwrites param_groups lr with the stage's configured value. R3 does not change that ordering. R3 additionally RECORDS the pre-overwrite value, which production reports as production_lr_reports[...]['before'], and canonicalises it against the checkpoint's lr, so the restored learning rate is measured rather than merely declared to be unmeasurable. This is an addition to the evidence, not a change to the production path.

correction_4_what_must_still_be_detected.principle: the canonicalisation exists to remove a representational difference, not to remove the audit's teeth. Every corruption class below must still fail the gate, and each is listed with the mechanism that catches it.

classes.boolean_flip: False and True convert to 0-D bool tensors whose single byte differs, so their sha256 differs. CAUGHT.
classes.boolean_versus_numeric_zero_dtype_confus: np.asarray(False) has dtype bool; np.asarray(0) has dtype int64. The canonical node carries the dtype, so ('t','bool',(),...) never equals ('t','int64',(),...). CAUGHT, and caught more sharply than under rev2, which could only distinguish them because bool took a different branch.
classes.changed_beta_eps_or_lr_beyond_the_effect: both sides are downcast to float32 by the same function; two values that differ in float32 produce different bytes. CAUGHT. A difference that does NOT survive float32 is not a difference the restore could have preserved, because RLlib's own conversion destroyed it before load_state_dict ever saw it; refusing to report it is a statement about the restore, not a tolerance applied to the comparison.
classes.dropped_or_added_key: the map branch compares the canonical key lists first and reports the asymmetric difference. CAUGHT.
classes.shortened_or_reordered_params: params is a list and canonicalises to ('seq', [...]), which preserves both length and order. CAUGHT.
classes.changed_state_index_set: the state dict's canonical key list changes, and the explicit state_indices comparison of rev3's predicate is retained unchanged. CAUGHT twice.
classes.changed_moment_value_dtype_or_shape: the tensor node carries dtype, shape and the sha256 of the bytes. CAUGHT. Moment tensors are float32 on both sides before and after conversion, so they stay BYTE-EXACT through canonicalisation: the conversion is a no-op for them and this is asserted, not assumed.

correction_4_what_must_still_be_detected.moments_must_stay_byte_exact: the predicate requires moment_digests_source and moment_digests_live, computed AFTER canonicalisation, to be equal element by element for all six indices and both moment keys, and additionally requires that canonicalisation did not alter either side's moment digests relative to their raw form. A canonicalisation that touched a moment would be a canonicalisation that had overreached.

correction_5_the_pass_must_be_evidential.why: a relaxed predicate and a correct predicate can produce the same boolean. The difference has to be visible in the artefact, otherwise the reader is asked to trust the implementation.

the_evidence_records_all_of.raw_provenance: both sides are ALSO normalised under rev2's exact rules, unchanged, and the resulting differences are recorded. On the state R2 measured this list must reproduce R2's eight strings exactly. Recording it makes R3 a superset of R2 rather than a replacement of it.
the_evidence_records_all_of.raw_leaf_values: for every path that differs raw, the evidence records the type and the repr of the value on BOTH sides, so a future reader can see what actually differed without re-running anything.
the_evidence_records_all_of.canonical_digests: a whole-tree canonical digest per side, a param_groups canonical digest per side, and the equality of each pair
the_evidence_records_all_of.canonical_differences: the full list, which must be empty
the_evidence_records_all_of.accepted_equivalences: the CLOSED list of paths that differ raw and agree canonically, each with both raw values and the canonical node they both collapse to. This list must equal EXACTLY the eight paths R2 measured. A ninth accepted equivalence is a change in the object under audit and is a PROBLEM, not a convenience.

correction_6_downstream_gates.the_observation: in R2, gates R3, R4, R6, R7 and R12 were reported as failures. None of them was an autonomous measurement. The wrapper raised inside _reapply_optimizer_learning_rate at train_ppo_mlp.py line 1744, which is called before line 1747 assigns restored_training_iteration and before the blocks that record actor_freeze_audit and critic_state_audit. Those five gates read fields that the aborted run never wrote.
correction_6_downstream_gates.why_this_matters: a gate that reads a field an aborted run never wrote has not measured anything. Reporting it as a failure alongside a genuine failure overstates how much went wrong and hides which single thing did.
correction_6_downstream_gates.the_rule: R3's runner computes live_restore_completed FIRST, from the child returncode, the summary stop_reason and the live evidence verdict. R3, R4, R6, R7 and R12 are EVALUATED only when live_restore_completed is true.
what_this_does_NOT_do: it does not make them pass. When they are not evaluated they are not passed, they do not count towards the passed total, and the verdict is still FAIL_CLOSED.
it does not change a single predicate. The predicates of R3, R4, R6, R7 and R12 are byte-identical to the base document's.
it does not suppress a genuine failure. If the live restore completed and one of the five then fails, it fails as an autonomous measurement and is reported as one.
correction_6_downstream_gates.how_it_is_recorded: the result records, per gate, evaluated true or false, passed true or false, and for a gate that was not evaluated the reason 'downstream of R9: the live restore did not complete, so the fields this gate reads were never written'. The receipt records gates_passed, gates_total, gates_failed and gates_not_evaluated separately.
